chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, who said:

I entered upon Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), and before her was a tablet in which were the names of the successors from her offspring. So I counted twelve; the last of them was al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام). Three of them were named Muḥammad, and three of them were named ʿAlī.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: al-Qāʾim, the one who will arise
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ: Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), daughter of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.لَوْحٌ: a tablet or inscribed board containing written names

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Fāṭimah’s tablet say about the twelve successors?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī saw a tablet before Fāṭimah (عليها السلام) containing the names of the successors from her progeny. It states that they were twelve in number, ending with al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام), and identifies recurring names among them. In Shia tradition, the report is significant as a textual affirmation of the line of the twelve Imams.
